headline: 7y auction 5.085%, highest since 1993, claims 197K, MOVE above 100, Dow's 4th down week
stance: Strong data and a weak 7y auction pushed the long end to 20-year highs. Credit widened, equity vol did not.

news.head: $44bn 7-year auction tailed at a 33-year high yield
news.body: Thursday's sale cleared 5.085%, the highest since April 1993. Cover fell to 2.42 from 2.50. Indirect bidders took 57.2%, down from 61%.

news.head: Jobless claims 197K, near 57-year lows
news.body: Reported Thursday, down 1,000 on the week. The four-week average fell to 202,250. Nothing in the labor data slows the repricing.

news.head: New home sales rose 6.4% in August to 684,000
news.body: Reported Thursday, 11% above forecast and the highest since December 2025. The Midwest and South rose; the Northeast and West fell.

news.head: Brent above $106 on Iran escalation threat
news.body: Brent rose more than 3% Thursday. An Iranian military official said Tehran could widen the war to the Indian Ocean.

implications: Demand is setting the long end, not the Fed. Two auctions tailed in two days.
Quarter-end is Wednesday and funding is already pricing. That is next week's risk, not duration.

watch.head: Durable goods orders, 8:30
watch.body: Advance August orders, forecast -0.3% after +1.1%. A capex beat pushes the long end the same way the auctions did.

watch.head: Consumer sentiment final, 10:00
watch.body: Household inflation expectations matter more than the headline. Fuel is up and the flash survey showed input costs rising.

watch.head: JOLTS, Sep 29
watch.body: Labor demand rather than headcount, at 10:00 Tuesday. PCE and GDP follow Wednesday.

watch.head: Quarter-end funding into Wednesday
watch.body: Reserves, the Treasury account and commercial paper all moved this week. Watch whether the turn passes quietly.

sections.title: Macro & Rates
bullets: Second straight day higher at the long end. The 20y and 30y closed Thursday above any level in 20 years.
MOVE above 100 Thursday, first time since March. It sat at 78.6 on Tuesday.
Breakevens fell Thursday while real yields rose. Thursday's move was entirely real.
sections.positioning: September 15 report: specs turned extended long Canadian dollar at the 88th percentile, new this week.

sections.title: Equity Markets
bullets: The Dow is down a fourth straight week. The Nasdaq-100 is up 1.6% since last Friday.
S&P breadth fell to 27.5% above the 50-day Thursday, the lowest since March.
Nasdaq breadth rose to 45.5% the same day. Participation is splitting by index, not just price.

single_name.note: Inhibrx Biosciences: two insider buy rules fired on Wednesday's filing. 10.4 days to cover, above its 200-day. Top score on the screen.

sections.title: Credit & Liquidity
bullets: High yield widened Wednesday against flat investment grade. Credit has now answered the rate move.
The Treasury account gained $100bn last week and reserves lost $84bn. Reverse repo cannot absorb the turn.
The commercial paper spread is 19bp this week from 2bp last week. Quarter-end funding is pricing.
